findings.text: Provides guest readable capability words for common performance events, with one selector choosing lower versus upper half. Caller supplies a vCPU and a half selector and receives a filtered capability word.
Manages per CPU accumulations of performance monitoring events wanted on host and on guest. One operation adds requested bits unless excluded, the other removes bits from both accumulations.
Exposes host side propagation of the user enable register and a request to resynchronize guest trap state for that register. Both depend on virtualization extensions and current execution context.
Distributes a software generated interrupt requested by one vCPU to selected recipient vCPUs, honoring broadcast versus affinity targeting and caller supplied group permission.

Capability words combine host PMU common and extended bitmaps converted to thirty two bit halves, pairing matching halves into sixty four bits. Lower half always advertises software increment and chain support, while upper half suppresses three stall related events when strict virtualization is not enabled. When a VM filter exists, the result is further restricted by mask bytes gathered from two bitmap regions.

Decisions to track events depend on PMU version support and on exclusion attributes. With host extensions and user exclusion no switch is needed, otherwise need follows inequality of host versus guest exclusion. Accumulation adds only when relevant side is included, while clearing removes from both sides when version support exists.

User enable propagation succeeds only with version support plus host extensions, a running vCPU, and an on CPU marker, storing the supplied value into host context. Resynchronization is requested only with host extensions in interrupt context and a running vCPU.

Guest page table dump state bundles a second stage MMU pointer, a generic page dump parser, two address markers delimiting one guest range, and one descriptor per page table level sized by maximum level count.

Display table associates validity, read permission, write permission, four execute permission combinations, access flag, and block versus page distinction with short human readable markers. Aggregation of all masks yields the significant bit set for dumping.

Level descriptors are validated against the last level, share one common mask and bit table, and carry numeric names. Parser allocation initializes from the page table start level, labels the first marker for guest intermediate addresses, and terminates the second marker at the address space top.

Visitor records each leaf address with its level and prior entry value into dump state and reports success. Guest display walks from zero across two raised to address size using leaf only visitation with initial level negative one.
Guest range display holds the VM memory management lock in write mode for the whole walk and flush sequence, serializing against concurrent table mutations.

Software interrupt queuing and private interrupt enable synchronization serialize per interrupt state with a raw spin lock held with interrupts saved, covering group checks, pending updates, enable flag writes, and host injection calls.

Guest dump file exposes open read seek and release operations. Open acquires a safe VM reference and allocates parser state, show walks the full intermediate range and flushes coalesced output, close frees state and drops the reference.

Two companion debug files report address size and active level count respectively. Their opens share a common helper that pins the VM and binds the page table pointer, while closes release the reference. All use sequential file read and seek helpers.
Intermediate address limit and host plus maximum vector length controls are initialization time globals that become read only after early setup.

Trap handlers signal handled with true and unhandled undefined injection with false. Direction mismatches funnel through a common unexpected trap that warns once and prints the encoding before injecting undefined. Helpers cover empty message printing, silent write ignoring, and zero returning reads.

Register placement uses flag bits distinguishing memory residence, CPU loaded, mapped to another CPU register, translated width, and demanding special handling. Each located register records placement flags, an alternate vCPU register selector when mapped, and an optional value translation callback.

General registers support symmetric read write access, while cache maintenance traps accept only writes and record a way flush need when firmware coherency support is absent. Tagged memory variant adds a feature gate before delegating. Virtual memory controls merge partial writes preserving untouched portions and reevaluate cache state against prior enablement. Auxiliary controls ignore writes and return masked shifted portions on reads, with helper selecting low high or full width portions.

Guest interrupt sender traps require interrupt controller version three and write direction, decoding target group from architecture dependent opcode fields. Dispatch extracts the interrupt identity, broadcasts to all other vCPUs when routing mode is set, otherwise reconstructs affinity from three levels plus target list and resolves each recipient via MPIDR lookup before queuing subject to group permission.

System register emulation gates controller accesses on version three, ignores enable writes while returning fixed hypervisor versus per CPU values for status reads, and deactivates on directory writes. Read as zero write ignored behavior covers miscellaneous traps. Newer controller version composes identifier priority and width fields, derives affinity from vCPU identity, and merges guest private enable writes with an architectural mask before syncing per interrupt enable flags.

Limited ordering region traps require feature presence, forbid writes to the identifier, and otherwise behave as zero on read and ignored on write. Operating system lock sender accepts only writes and forwards to debug handling, status register is read only from stored state with userspace mutation restricted to one lock bit, authentication status ignores writes and passes through host value on reads, and general debug registers perform normal access then transfer ownership to the guest.

Invalid start levels, unexpected register directions, and unexpected enable reads trigger once only warnings. Hardware backed interrupt injection failures are rate limited warnings. Allocation exhaustion and failure to pin the VM abort open paths with negative error codes without leaking references.
Address marker array holds two entries.
Cache size selection upper bound is fourteen.
Maximum page table level count equals last level index plus one.
Second stage filename buffer accommodates two hexadecimal addresses plus a disabled suffix.
Lower capability half uses event base zero and upper half uses base thirty two, with filter bytes also consulted at an offset sixteen thousand above each base and assembled eight bits at a time.
Range file presents address bit count and levels file presents active level count, each as decimal text.

Dump session moves from allocation through level setup to sequential display under lock and finally to teardown. Failures at allocation or setup release prior resources and propagate errors, successful display always flushes pending output before returning.

Queuing first checks group zero versus group one permission, dropping disallowed requests. Allowed software interrupts set a latched pending flag and join the virtual queue, while allowed hardware backed interrupts request pending state from the host controller. Reference is always released after unlocking.
